question.text: What 2026 cumulative dengue case count will Colombia's INS report in the latest weekly epidemiological bulletin published on or before 27 November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the year-to-date 2026 dengue case total reported in the most recent issue of Colombia's Boletín Epidemiológico Semanal (BES, Instituto Nacional de Salud) posted on the INS website on or before 27 November 2026 (Colombia local time, UTC−5). Issues are reachable via the INS BES portal at https://www.ins.gov.co/publicaciones/SitePages/BES.aspx; the latest issue published as of mid-November 2026 is the one for epidemiological week 43 (25–31 October 2026), and the resolving issue will normally be the week 46 issue (15–21 November 2026), or the week 45 issue (8–14 November 2026) if week 46 is not posted in time. The resolved value is the bulletin's accumulated dengue total for 2026 — the combined figure covering all clinical classifications (dengue without warning signs, with warning signs, and severe dengue) shown alongside the week's new dengue case count in the bulletin's national-situation / tracer-events entry for dengue, whether that cumulative is labelled by epidemiological week or by epidemiological period (the week-43 issue reported 97,894). Report the value in cases (e.g. 97,894 resolves as 97,894). If the INS bulletin cannot be retrieved, the figure reported for that bulletin by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) may be used.
question.fine_print: An issue counts as published on the date it is posted on the INS website; a week-46 issue posted after 23:59 Colombia time (UTC−5) on 27 November 2026 does not count, and the week-45 issue is used instead. If the INS portal gives no posting date for an issue, use the publication date printed on the bulletin itself or, failing that, the earliest date on which the issue was publicly available (e.g. the first web-archive capture). If a single bulletin presents different accumulated dengue totals in different places (for example the national command table, "Tabla de mando nacional", versus the dengue section), use the dengue-section figure described above.

research:
The latest figure is the week-44 bulletin's: **102,164 cases** (EW44, 1-7 November). That is 4,270 more than week 43. I could not open the bulletin itself because the INS site was unreachable. The number comes from press reports dated 17 November.

## 1. Resolution source
- I could not reach the INS BES portal or any INS bulletin PDF from my tools ("Network is unreachable"). The week-44 file is indexed at [2026_Boletin_epidemiologico_semana_44.pdf](https://www.ins.gov.co/buscador-eventos/BoletinEpidemiologico/2026_Boletin_epidemiologico_semana_44.pdf), so it has been posted, but I don't know the posting date.
- 2026-11-17: Diario del Sur says the INS reported 102,164 cumulative dengue cases through week 44 (1-7 November), 1,023 of them severe, with the national picture still "in outbreak". I only saw this in search snippets; both articles returned HTTP 403. [Diario del Sur](http://diariodelsur.com.co/noticias/ins-reporta-102-164-casos-de-dengue-en-colombia-hasta-noviembre), [Diario del Sur 2](http://diariodelsur.com.co/noticias/colombia-enciende-las-alarmas-dengue-supera-los-102-000-casos-y-preocupa-el-aumento)
- I could not find the week-44 split between new and late notifications, or its death count.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing is settled yet. The deciding issue will be week 46, expected around 26-27 November, or week 45 if week 46 is late. To land inside the 97,000-111,000 range, growth from 102,164 would have to stay under about 4,400 a week over two weeks.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-17: Diario del Sur reports the week-44 total of 102,164 (see above).
- 2026-11-16: El Espectador cites the INS at **102,415 cases as of 10 November**, with 76 confirmed deaths and 31 under study. This looks like a different cut from the bulletin, perhaps a dashboard or Sivigila figure. It says 41% of deaths were in people aged 5 to 19. [El Espectador](https://www.elespectador.com/salud/otra-vez-el-dengue-mas-de-100-000-casos-y-una-respuesta-que-sigue-en-deuda/)
- 2026-11-17: Researchers report dengue serotypes 2, 3 and 4 circulating in Barranquilla and Atlántico. [El Heraldo](https://www.elheraldo.co/atlantico/barranquilla/2026/11/17/rastrean-los-virus-que-causan-fiebre-en-barranquilla-y-municipios-del-atlantico/)
- 2026-11-10: The Ministry of Health reported 98,096 cases and 73 confirmed deaths (from the question background, also cited by Diario del Sur).
- 2026-11-06: The week-43 bulletin reported 97,894 cases. By classification: 59,472 without warning signs, 37,443 with warning signs, 979 severe. Deaths were 65 confirmed and 45 under investigation. Leading departments: Meta 14,131, Bolívar 9,704, Santander 7,488. [Noticias RCN](https://www.noticiasrcn.com/salud-y-bienestar/dengue-colombia-casos-muertes-recomendaciones-1079432), [Blu Radio](https://www.bluradio.com/salud/dengue-en-colombia-casi-98-mil-contagios-y-65-muertes-confirmadas-rg10)
- 2026-10-19: Reports cite 83,382 cases and 46 deaths under study. [Radio Hoy](https://www.radiohoy.com/2026/10/19/dengue-en-colombia-alertan-por-83-382-contagios-y-46-muertes-en-estudio/826569/)
- 2026-11-16: PAHO says the Americas are 53% below 2025 for the year, but Colombia is running against that regional trend. [ReliefWeb/PAHO](https://reliefweb.int/report/brazil/dengue-epidemiological-situation-region-americas-epidemiological-week-42-2026)

## 4. Base rates
- **2026 weekly increases in the cumulative total:** EW31 to EW32 +1,980; EW32 to EW38 about +2,200 a week; EW38 to EW42 about +2,770 a week; EW42 to EW43 +3,276; **EW43 to EW44 +4,270**. The increases have grown every week from EW38 onward.
- **Simple projections:** two more weeks at +3,000 to +4,500 each would put the EW46 total at about 108,000-111,000. The EW45 total, if week 46 slips, would be about 105,000-106,700. Adding the 2026 mean of about 2,800 a week would give about 107,800.
- **2025 at the same time of year:** 106,541 at EW39 (4 October) and 117,789 by 2 December, about 1,400-1,600 a week through the late season. 2025 ended at about 123,800. [Portafolio](https://www.portafolio.co/economia/regiones/dengue-en-colombia-mas-de-106-000-casos-y-131-muertes-en-2025-segun-el-ins-642201), [Portafolio](https://www.portafolio.co/economia/regiones/colombia-acumula-117-789-casos-de-dengue-con-141-muertes-notificadas-segun-el-ins-484477)
  - 2026 has been adding roughly twice 2025's weekly pace and is closing the gap with last year.
  - Late November usually brings slowing or steady weekly counts after the second-half rains. I could not get national EW44 to EW46 figures for 2022-2024 because the INS PDFs would not open.
- **Late notifications:** in the week-43 report, 1,175 of 3,821 notifications (31%) were for earlier weeks. Back-filling adds to every increase.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on Colombia's dengue count. The Kalshi Florida dengue market and the other listed markets are unrelated.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 19-20 November: the week-45 bulletin (8-14 November) is expected.
- About 26-27 November: the week-46 bulletin (15-21 November) is expected; this is the likely resolving issue.
- Weather: IDEAM declared El Niño conditions on 8 October, and the government says this raises dengue risk. I did not find a newer IDEAM outlook. The Ministry of Health has stepped up vector control, but I found no evidence it has bent the curve yet: increases were still accelerating through week 44.
- Small risk: the 102,164 figure comes from press, not the bulletin, and El Espectador's 102,415 shows that different INS cuts exist. Check the week-45 and week-46 PDFs directly if you can reach them.

# Colombia dengue: research notes for the week 45/46 INS bulletin (as of 2026-11-18)

**Key finding:** the week 44 bulletin has already been published. It reports **102,164** cumulative 2026 cases, up 4,270 from 97,894 in week 43. That is the largest weekly jump in the recent run. The question is not settled yet: the resolving issue (week 46, or week 45 if week 46 is late) has not been published.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-18: I could not reach the INS BES portal: the connection failed. I also could not open the week 44 PDF, although search found it at [INS BES semana 44](https://www.ins.gov.co/buscador-eventos/BoletinEpidemiologico/2026_Boletin_epidemiologico_semana_44.pdf), and search showed only its cover and index. The week 43 PDF is at the [same path](https://www.ins.gov.co/buscador-eventos/BoletinEpidemiologico/2026_Boletin_epidemiologico_semana_43.pdf). I found no CSV or JSON data behind the portal.
- Latest value: week 44 (1-7 Nov 2026) = **102,164** cumulative cases, 1,023 of them severe dengue, according to the BES as reported by Diario del Sur on 2026-11-17. [Diario del Sur](http://diariodelsur.com.co/noticias/ins-reporta-102-164-casos-de-dengue-en-colombia-hasta-noviembre)
- I could not find the week 44 bulletin's breakdown of the 4,270 increase into cases from week 44 itself versus late notifications from earlier weeks.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The week 45 issue is expected around 19-20 Nov and the week 46 issue around 26-27 Nov.
- Week 44 shows the national situation still in outbreak. Notifications in weeks 40-43 were **40.6% above** weeks 36-39, up from +33.8% in the previous comparison (weeks 39-42 vs 35-38). [Diario del Sur](http://diariodelsur.com.co/noticias/ins-reporta-102-164-casos-de-dengue-en-colombia-hasta-noviembre)
- A second figure is in circulation: El Espectador (2026-11-16) cites INS at **102,415 cases with a 10 November cutoff**, plus 76 confirmed and 31 under-investigation deaths. This is probably a dashboard or SIVIGILA figure, not the BES number. Its existence suggests the running count was already above 102.4k on 10 Nov. [El Espectador](https://www.elespectador.com/salud/otra-vez-el-dengue-mas-de-100-000-casos-y-una-respuesta-que-sigue-en-deuda/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-17: Researchers from Unisimón and George Washington University found serotypes 2, 3 and 4 circulating in Barranquilla and Atlántico. [El Heraldo](https://www.elheraldo.co/atlantico/barranquilla/2026/11/17/rastrean-los-virus-que-causan-fiebre-en-barranquilla-y-municipios-del-atlantico/)
- 2026-11-17: Diario del Sur reports the week 44 BES at 102,164 cases, 1,023 severe; Nariño has 711 cases. [Diario del Sur](http://diariodelsur.com.co/noticias/colombia-enciende-las-alarmas-dengue-supera-los-102-000-casos-y-preocupa-el-aumento)
- 2026-11-16: El Espectador reports 102,415 cases at 10 Nov, 107 deaths in total, and 41% of deaths among people aged 5-19. [El Espectador](https://www.elespectador.com/salud/otra-vez-el-dengue-mas-de-100-000-casos-y-una-respuesta-que-sigue-en-deuda/)
- 2026-11-06: The week 43 BES reported 97,894 cases and 65 confirmed deaths. [Noticias RCN](https://www.noticiasrcn.com/salud-y-bienestar/dengue-colombia-casos-muertes-recomendaciones-1079432), [Blu Radio](https://www.bluradio.com/salud/dengue-en-colombia-casi-98-mil-contagios-y-65-muertes-confirmadas-rg10)

## 4. Base rates
Recent BES cumulative totals in 2026:

| Week | Cumulative cases | Change |
|---|---|---|
| EW38 | 83,556 | |
| EW42 | 94,618 | about +2,765 per week over EW38-42 |
| EW43 | 97,894 | +3,276 |
| EW44 | 102,164 | **+4,270** |

- Weekly increases are getting bigger, not smaller.
- Simple arithmetic, not a forecast: adding 3,000-4,500 per week to 102,164 gives about 105-107k for week 45 and about 108-111k for week 46. The top of that range reaches the question's upper bound of 111,000.

Seasonal comparison with 2025, using sparse press figures:
- About 106,541 cases at the end of October 2025, and 117,789 at a 2 December 2025 cutoff. That is roughly 11,250 cases over about 4.5 weeks, or about 2,500 per week through November. [Portafolio Oct 2025](https://www.portafolio.co/economia/regiones/dengue-en-colombia-mas-de-106-000-casos-y-131-muertes-en-2025-segun-el-ins-642201), [Portafolio Dec 2025](https://www.portafolio.co/economia/regiones/colombia-acumula-117-789-casos-de-dengue-con-141-muertes-notificadas-segun-el-ins-484477)
- 2025 ended at about 123,800.
- 2026's weekly increases (about 3,300-4,300) are now above 2025's November pace, and the cumulative gap is narrowing.
- I could not find national week 45/46 figures for 2022-2024.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on this question.
- The Kalshi Florida dengue market and the other markets supplied are unrelated.
- PAHO's week 42 report gives the regional context: cases across the Americas are down 53% year on year. [ReliefWeb/PAHO](https://reliefweb.int/report/brazil/dengue-epidemiological-situation-region-americas-epidemiological-week-42-2026)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 19-20 Nov: the week 45 BES (8-14 Nov), which is the fallback resolving issue.
- About 26-27 Nov: the week 46 BES (15-21 Nov), the expected resolving issue. Publication dates have varied by up to a day (for example, week 41 came out on a Friday, 23 Oct). A delay past 23:59 Colombia time on 27 Nov would make week 45 the resolving issue.
- Weather: IDEAM declared El Niño conditions on 8 Oct, and the government cites this as raising dengue risk. I did not find an updated IDEAM outlook for late November. Vector control has been stepped up, but the week 44 data does not yet show a slowdown.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 9 days. The resolving bulletin (EW46, 15-21 November) should be posted around 26-27 November 2026. If it slips past 27 November, the EW45 issue resolves instead.

(b) **Latest known value:** 102,164 cumulative cases in the EW44 bulletin (1-7 November). This comes from press reports dated 17 November, not from the bulletin itself, which my assistant could not open.

(c) **If nothing changed:** 102,164. That is not realistic, because the total rises by thousands of cases every week.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** Weekly increases have grown every week: about 2,770 a week over EW38-42, then 3,276, then 4,270.
- If the next two weeks add about 4,000-4,800 each, EW46 lands at about 110,000-111,800.
- If growth slows to about 3,500 a week, EW46 is about 109,200.
- If EW46 slips and EW45 resolves, the value is about 106,000-107,000.

(e) **Historical variation:** Over two weeks the cumulative total moves about 4,000-10,000 cases.
- Late-season increases in 2025 were about 1,400-1,600 a week.
- 2026 is running at about twice that, and still accelerating.
- Back-filled late notifications add about 30% to each week's increase.

(f) **Experts and markets:** There are no markets or expert forecasts on this quantity. The question creator's range is 97,000-111,000. My central estimate sits near the top of that range.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- *Low outcome:* EW46 is posted late and EW45 resolves, or the weekly increases fall back sharply (seasonal decline or vector control taking effect). This gives about 104,000-106,000.
- *High outcome:* The outbreak keeps accelerating under El Niño and a large batch of late notifications arrives. Increases of 5,500-6,500 a week would give about 114,000-116,000 or more.
